BLIND arm. Answered only from documented biography (Wikipedia main article + 'Health and appearance of Michael Jackson' + 'Personal relationships of Michael Jackson' + 'Death of Michael Jackson' + 'Neverland Ranch' + 'Jackson family'; Britannica, CNN, CNBC/Billboard/Time on the finances, People v. Jackson coverage, Quincy Jones and Taraborrelli characterisations, Find a Grave/FamilySearch for grandparents). Part D omitted - this exercise forbade opening any reading, and no astrology source of any kind was consulted. Born 29 Aug 1958, St Mary's Mercy Hospital, Gary, Indiana; died 25 Jun 2009, Los Angeles, age 50, acute propofol intoxication ruled homicide (Conrad Murray convicted of involuntary manslaughter, Nov 2011).

Genuinely uncertain / conservative picks:
A1-A3 - the widely circulated '7:33 pm' figure has no primary source I could verify from biography alone; its only carriers are astrological databases and fan reposts, which this arm may not use. 'unknown' three times is the honest answer, not a research gap.
A7/A8 - no biographer records a sickly infancy or a life-threatening event before age eight; the documented childhood suffering is beatings by Joe, exhaustion and (from adolescence) acne. 'average' and 'no' are the conservative reads, both weakly sourced.
A9 - all four grandparents traced: Samuel Joseph Jackson 1893-1993 (100), Crystal Lee King 1907-1992 (85), Prince Albert Scruse 1907-1997 (90), Martha Mattie Upshaw 1907-1990 (83). Mean 89.5, so '80_90' rather than 'over90'.
A11 - 'prospered' is the trajectory, not the start: Joe was a US Steel crane operator with a second job at American Foundries and Katherine worked part-time at Sears, in a two-bedroom house on Jackson Street; the Motown deal (Mar 1969) and four consecutive #1s in 1970 made the family wealthy while Michael was 10-11. Early childhood alone would read 'steady'.
A13 - single-choice forces one label on a mixed record: Jermaine's 1991 diss record 'Word to the Badd!!', La Toya's 1993 televised accusations (later recanted), his 1984 split from the brothers, and a will that left the siblings nothing, against real closeness in childhood and public family support at the 2005 trial. 'conflicted' is the best-supported single label. A brother, Brandon (Marlon's twin), died the day after birth in Mar 1957, before Michael was born, so 'lost' would misdescribe a lived loss.
A14 - withdrawn from Gardner Street Elementary c.1970 and taught by private tutor Rose Fine; only a brief stint at Montclair College Prep. Reports of a 1975 Montclair diploma exist but I could not confirm them from a reputable source, so 'school' rather than 'higher_secondary'. His Fisk University doctorate (1988) was honorary and does not count.
A16/A17/A18 - he was a contracted recording artist, not a salaried employee; MJJ Productions, the ATV/Sony-ATV publishing stake and the touring operation make 'own_business' the only fitting code. 'religious' is selected for the charitable arm (We Are the World 1985, Heal the World Foundation, an estimated $500m given away), not for clergy work.
A21 - no documented gambling or lottery. 'net_gain' rests on the $47.5m ATV catalogue purchase (Aug 1985), an equity bet whose half-share the estate later sold for around $750m - the largest documented speculative gain of his life. If the question is read strictly as betting, 'never' would be the alternative.
A23 - 'serious_now' means at end of life: reporting at his death put him roughly $400-500m in debt, spending $20-30m a year more than he earned, with Neverland saved from foreclosure in May 2008 only by Colony Capital buying the defaulted $24.5m loan.
A25/A26/A27 - Lisa Marie Presley m. 26 May 1994, separated 10 Dec 1995, divorce final 20 Aug 1996; Debbie Rowe m. 15 Nov 1996, divorced Apr 2000. Married first at 35, against parents who married at 21 and 19 and brothers who married in their late teens and early twenties, hence 'late'. Both marriages ended.
A29 - 'yes' rests on Debbie Rowe's miscarriage in March 1996, documented on the relationships page; his third child (Feb 2002) was carried by an unnamed surrogate.
A30 - Quincy Jones described him as 'introverted, shy, and nonassertive'; colleagues describe a soft-spoken man who avoided large gatherings and worked in long solitary stretches, which gives reserved and solitary. 'bold' is for the documented artistic and business risk-taking (the moonwalk debut, the ATV bid, the 37% royalty). 'philosophical' for the Witness upbringing and the humanitarian/metaphysical register of his own writing. No source supports quick_tempered.
A31 - 'extended': antidepressants and depression attested by his daughter, chronic insomnia worsening from the 1996 HIStory tour, the Nov 1993 painkiller dependency and roughly two months of rehabilitation abroad, and the propofol regimen of 2009.
A33/A34 - Gary to Los Angeles in 1969, Neverland 1988-2005, then about a year in Bahrain and several months in Ireland after the acquittal, so 'abroad'. Confinement was real but short: hospitalisations, the 1993 rehab stay, no custodial sentence (booked and released Nov 2003).
A35 - twelve-row cap forced omissions. Also dated and not listed: 1964 joined the Jackson Brothers; Mar 1969 Motown contract; 1975 move to Epic; 28 Feb 1984 eight Grammys in one night; 1987-88 Bad tour records; Nov 1996 second marriage; 3 Apr 1998 and 21 Feb 2002 children; Feb 2003 Bashir documentary; 20 Nov 2003 arrest; Feb 2008 Neverland foreclosure notice; 5 Mar 2009 This Is It announcement; 25 Jun 2009 death.
A36 - he died in 2009, so 'the time since mid-2023' has no first-person referent; 'same' is the null answer rather than a claim about posthumous estate fortunes.
B1 - opt1: every contemporaneous description is of a highly impressionable, easily moved man who withdrew under pressure and returned, with a very small close circle - the opposite of opt2's wide circle.
B2/B3 - 5'9", 136 lb at autopsy, lifelong slenderness; universally read as younger than his age.
B4 - eighth of ten surviving-into-childhood siblings, so 'middle'.
B6 - father_death and mother_death are unanswerable in the required sense: Joe Jackson died in 2018 and Katherine outlived him, so neither occurred within his lifetime and both rows are omitted rather than guessed. own_surgery is dated to the scalp surgeries following the 27 Jan 1984 Pepsi burn, the first surgery with a firm public date; he admitted two earlier rhinoplasties whose dates are not documented.
C-section reasoning: C1 both (the most-awarded entertainer in history and the most publicly disgraced). C2/C11 clearly difficult (discoid lupus diagnosed 1983, vitiligo 1986 and confirmed at autopsy, degenerative lumbar and finger osteoarthritis, chronic interstitial pneumonitis, chronic insomnia; two failed marriages). C3 difficult (extortion claims, tabloid war, two criminal investigations, litigation from former associates). C4 difficult on balance - Neverland was a twenty-year sanctuary but ended in raid, abandonment, default and a post-mortem sale far below its asking price; confidence only 3. C5 low confidence: no documented vehicle trouble at all, so 'gone well' is close to a null answer. C6 both - his voice was his supreme asset and also the recurring failure point (laryngitis 1988, swollen vocal cords, cancelled shows 1988 and 1992). C7 difficult - marriages ended, the Sony relationship turned openly hostile in 2002, promoters and former managers sued; the Quincy Jones partnership is the strong counter-example, hence confidence 3. C9 difficult - the 1993 settlement ($23m, Jan 1994), the 2003-05 prosecution ending in acquittal on all counts (13 Jun 2005), and posthumous allegations left his conduct permanently contested despite the acquittal and the philanthropy. C10 gone well - record-breaking world tours and most of his income earned far from Gary, discounted to confidence 3 because the Dangerous tour collapsed mid-run in Nov 1993. C12 both - Neverland and the Bahrain exile were refuge and cage at once.
